IDENTIFIABILITY_of_the_N_curve.why: selfcons_slots.py measured that 6 of 17 pools are NOT slot-exchangeable. On such a pool 'N=2' is ambiguous: a random 2-subset of the 8-fan and the FIRST 2 slots of the fan are different experiments. The spread between the three conventions is reported per cell per N; where it exceeds the effect, the N point is NOT IDENTIFIED and no claim is made at that N.
IDENTIFIABILITY_of_the_N_curve.headline: on PMC_VQA at N=2 the delta is -0.0190 for a random 2-subset of the fan and +0.0193 for the first 2 slots of the same fan -- a SIGN FLIP of 0.038 from nothing but which two samples you get. N=8 uses the whole pool and is invariant to all three conventions, so it is the only budget at which this cell's number means anything.

VERDICT.consequence: for any pool listed above, an index tie-break carries a position bias and the N-curve must also be reported with an ORDER-FREE tie-break (random among the tied classes). selfcons_suite.py reports index, order-free and first-N-prefix.
VERDICT.MEASURED_not_inferred: the permutation test, the per-slot marginals, the per-slot token counts and the per-slot greedy agreement are all measurements in this file.
VERDICT.HYPOTHESIS_not_measured: the pattern is CONSISTENT WITH a fixed per-request seed making the n sequences a fixed QUANTILE FAN rather than n i.i.d. draws: the per-slot agreement with greedy is a stable per-slot constant, the deviation is in the ANSWER-SPACE MARGINAL and not in length, and the effect is large where the answer is essentially one token drawn from a small biased space (PMC letters, PATH_VQA yes/no) and washes out on multi-token open text. THIS MECHANISM IS NOT PROVEN HERE. Proving it needs an A/B of one fixed seed versus per-request seeds, which is a GPU job and was not run.

MACRO8_consequence.how: five of the eight cells are untouched (their published value IS a real greedy decode); the three open cells move by the measured per-cell difference. The macro is the equal-weight mean over eight cells, so the shift is (sum of the three per-cell differences) / 8, bootstrapped by resampling items inside each of the three moving cells.
MACRO8_consequence.and_it_is_cheaper: the corrected baseline is a REAL greedy decode on all eight cells, so it costs 1.0 FLOP-eq, against 1.513738 for the published one.
MACRO8_consequence.read_as_an_intervention: stated the other way round: DELETING self-consistency from the three open cells of the published baseline is the cheapest intervention this round found -- it moves the macro UP and cuts baseline compute by a third.

CONSEQUENCE_cost.arithmetic: five cells at 1.0 plus three cells at the measured 2.369969 = 1.513738
CONSEQUENCE_cost.read: the baseline every arm in this round is measured against is not a 1.0 FLOP-eq baseline. It is a 1.51 FLOP-eq baseline under the project's own measured generation cost, because three of its eight cells already pay for eight samples.

THE_PUBLISHED_OPEN_CELL_BASELINE_IS_ALRE.WHAT_IS_NOT_CLAIMED: this does NOT say any published DELTA is wrong. Every arm in the open-cell chain (verifier, head, oracle) was compared against the same greedy_ok field, so the deltas are internally consistent. What is wrong is the LABEL on the baseline and the 1.0 charged for it.
